newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch insurers seen continuing outperformance.
newsitem.headline: Dutch insurers seen continuing outperformance.

text.p: Dutch insurance shares are set for a strong rise over the next year after playing catch-up with their European counterparts in recent years, but the scope for further outperformance beyond that is limited, analysts said.

They said Dutch insurance firms' shares were likely to rise by at least 10 percent, although some believed Aegon was fairly valued after gaining nearly 60 percent in 1995 and another 25 percent this year.
"Aegon is a great business," said analyst Stephan Dias of Goldman Sachs. "The only problem is the share price."
While London-based Dias is keeping Aegon at a hold, Michael Lindsay of Lehman Brothers has switched it to a sell. "Aegon is overvalued, nevertheless it's a very good stock," Lindsay said.
"Other Dutch insurance stocks should gain another 10 percent by the end of this year or in the start of 1997," he added, naming ING and Fortis Amev as good buys.

While the return on equity (capital gains plus dividends) of many European insurance companies needed to improve, Aegon, ING and Fortis Amev had all shown excellent figures and analysts forecasted strong figures from them in the near future.
A recent BZW reseach note shows an estimated 11.3 percent return on equity for ING in 1996 and 11.1 percent for 1997.
Aegon's return on equity was estimated at 15.7 in 1996 and 16.0 percent for the year after, while Fortis Amev was likely to show returns of 12.9 percent in 1996 and 12.8 percent in 1997.

In the same report, BZW estimated that France's AXA would show a return on equity of 7.7 percent in 1996 and 8.1 percent in 1997, with Germany's Allianz returning an estimated 3.7 percent in 1996 and 3.9 percent in 1997.

"Dutch insurance firms have been succesfull in cutting costs in the last few years, have improved the quality of their earnings, have done better acquisitions and did not issue new shares," Dias said, adding there were good reasons for the sector's outstanding performance in the sharemarket.
While Angus Runciman of BZW Research has a neutral stance on the European insurance sector, he remains upbeat on ING, Fortis Amev and Aegon, giving them all a buy recommendation.
But he could not follow the logic of Fortis' latest move, the signing of a letter of intent two weeks ago to buy Dutch merchant bank MeesPierson from ABN AMRO.
"I have doubts about the strategy behind this move," said Runciman, adding Fortis had focused on retail banking, savings and insurance until now.
Michael Lindsay of Lehman Brothers also questioned the move.
"MeesPierson is not producing a very good return on equity. So why buy this business," he said, adding it would not help sentiment outside the Netherlands on Fortis.

In Runciman's view, ING has the best growth prospect among the three. "A combination of current value, growth prospects and visibility," he said, adding ING's intention to seek a bourse listing in the United States would also help if it proceeded.
Goldman Sachs' Dias is the most upbeat on ING's growth possibilities, expecting the price to rise by 15 percent in less than a year.

Analysts also note the Dutch economy should not show grow too strongly. "Otherwise interest rates might go up and this will not hold good news for insurance stocks," one said, adding cyclicals were more likely to gain if the economy picked up.
But recent Dutch inflation data was not worrying as inflation for September grew 2.0 percent year-on-year.
In the meantime, international insurance analysts also looked at other promising stocks in Europe.
They said Dutch insurance stocks were not overvalued yet but if their prices moved up another ten percent, it could be time to look further in Europe."

"I'm getting more and more enthusiastic about French companies like UAP and Axa," said Lindsay, adding Scandinavian, Swiss and German firms were also becoming attractive, while others mentioned French reinsurer Scor, Suez and German Allianz.
